body:
EXHAUSTIVE PWA/BROWSER CAPABILITY REPORT (official sources fetched in full; BCD current main branch checked 2026-08-13)

A. WINDOW MANAGEMENT / MULTI-DISPLAY
- API: `screen.isExtended` (multi-screen boolean, secure context, no permission prompt), `window.getScreenDetails()` (detailed screens; may prompt), `ScreenDetails.screens/currentScreen`, `screenschange`, `currentscreenchange`, per-screen `change`. Details include coordinates, work area, DPI, labels, primary/internal status. `getScreenDetails()` rejects `NotAllowedError` when Permissions Policy blocks `window-management` or user denies. Default Permissions-Policy allowlist is `self`; delegate iframe with `allow="window-management"`. Sources: W3C https://www.w3.org/TR/window-management/ ; MDN https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window_Management_API ; https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/getScreenDetails ; policy https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Permissions-Policy/window-management ; Chrome https://developer.chrome.com/docs/capabilities/web-apis/window-management
- Compatibility (MDN BCD): `getScreenDetails`, `screen.isExtended`, ScreenDetails landed Chrome 100 and Edge mirror; Firefox false; Safari false. Chrome Android reports API mirror for getScreenDetails/isExtended but ScreenDetails and events false; therefore product-grade target is Chromium desktop, not mobile. Permissions query descriptor `window-management` starts Chrome 111, false Firefox/Safari/Chrome Android. Raw BCD: https://github.com/mdn/browser-compat-data/blob/main/api/Window.json ; /Screen.json ; /ScreenDetails.json ; /Permissions.json
- Use feature detection (`'getScreenDetails' in window`), never UA detection. Handle denied permission and screen hot-plug/reconfiguration. Coordinates can be negative in virtual arrangements. `avail*` excludes OS UI and is the safer placement region.
- Exact product implication: extended mode is progressive enhancement. Chromium desktop can offer automatic stage placement; every other browser needs ordinary second-window/manual-drag or single-screen mode.

B. WINDOW.OPEN / POPUP RULES
- `window.open()` is broadly available, but browsers decide tab vs popup and may correct requested size/position to keep the whole popup inside an OS work area. It returns WindowProxy or `null` when popup blocked. New URL load is asynchronous; initial context is `about:blank`. Source: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/open
- Modern browsers require direct user input and a separate user gesture for each `window.open()` call. MDN Window Management usage explicitly recommends opening at most one new window at once, reusing named windows, and showing popup-blocker recovery instructions: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window_Management_API/Using
- Important narrow exception in Window Management spec: after a targeted fullscreen request, the spec permits one popup placement within the transient-activation interval, enabling fullscreen on one screen + one popup on another from one click. This does NOT license arbitrary fan-out. Source: https://www.w3.org/TR/window-management/
- Cross-origin stage placement works, but no DOM/function access. Restricted WindowProxy ordinarily retains close/closed/focus/blur/postMessage; COOP can sever it and make `closed === true`. Sources already sent in origin verdict.
- iOS BCD caveat: `window.open` partial; MDN BCD says it will not function if target is omitted or `_blank`, so use a stable named target if mobile fallback matters.

C. FULLSCREEN
- `Element.requestFullscreen()` requires transient user activation in the requesting document; it is also policy-controlled (`fullscreen`, default allowlist self). Users can always exit; support itself can be unavailable due to user preference, security risk, or platform limitation. Sources: WHATWG https://fullscreen.spec.whatwg.org/ ; MDN https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Fullscreen_API ; https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/requestFullscreen
- Window Management adds experimental `{screen: ScreenDetailed}` to target a display. Do not assume cross-browser support merely because `requestFullscreen()` supports an options object.
- Cross-origin implication: controller cannot invoke stage DOM fullscreen. WSS/postMessage does not transfer user activation. Cross-origin audience must expose its own local `Enter fullscreen` button/gesture. Sized placement is the fallback.
- Compatibility BCD for base requestFullscreen: modern Chrome 71+, Edge 79+, Firefox 64+, Safari 16.4+. iOS Safari 16.4 is iPad-only, not iPhone, shows a non-disableable overlay, and swipe-down exits; unsuitable as a guaranteed clean presentation surface. Raw: https://github.com/mdn/browser-compat-data/blob/main/api/Element.json
- Manifest `display: fullscreen` is separate from Fullscreen API; it controls installed-app launch display, can coexist with `document.fullscreenElement === null`, and falls back `fullscreen -> standalone -> minimal-ui -> browser`. Prefer `standalone` for control app, explicit Fullscreen API for stage. Source: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Progressive_web_apps/Manifest/Reference/display

D. PERMISSIONS MODEL
- Permissions API only reports aggregate state (`granted|denied|prompt`) across secure-context, Permissions Policy, interaction, and user choice. It does not itself grant and cannot revoke; `Permissions.revoke()` was removed. Listen to PermissionStatus `change`, and always still handle the actual API rejection. Sources: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Permissions_API ; https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Permissions/query ; spec https://www.w3.org/TR/permissions/
- Querying an unsupported descriptor rejects TypeError; catch it. Generic query support is Chrome 43+, Firefox 46+, Safari 16+, but individual descriptor support differs dramatically. `microphone` descriptor: Chrome 64+, Firefox 132+, Safari 16+. `window-management`: Chromium desktop only (Chrome 111+, Edge mirror). Raw BCD Permissions.json above.
- Permissions persist/revoke per browser policy and user settings; do not promise persistence. Query is status UX, actual invocation is authority.

E. MICROPHONE
- `navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia({audio:true})` is HTTPS/secure-context only; in insecure contexts `mediaDevices` is undefined. User permission is always required at least initially. Only top-level valid-origin documents may request unless top-level explicitly delegates `microphone` via Permissions Policy to iframe. Denial/policy/insecure failures commonly surface `NotAllowedError`; no matching device `NotFoundError`; unsatisfiable exact constraint `OverconstrainedError`; empty/all-false constraints TypeError; inactive document InvalidStateError. Source: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaDevices/getUserMedia ; spec https://w3c.github.io/mediacapture-main/
- Browsers must show mic-use indicator and granted-but-not-currently-recording indicator. Stop all tracks (`track.stop()`) immediately when listening ends; do not place mic in public stage origin.
- `enumerateDevices()` requires secure, fully active, visible document. Policy-blocked/ungranted devices are omitted; default devices appear first; non-default devices require permission and labels may be unavailable before grant. Source: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaDevices/enumerateDevices
- Compatibility BCD: getUserMedia Chrome 53+, Edge 12+, Firefox 36+, Safari 11+. Broad baseline; nevertheless actual device/OS denial must be first-class UI. Raw: https://github.com/mdn/browser-compat-data/blob/main/api/MediaDevices.json

F. SERVICE WORKERS / OFFLINE
- SW is an event-driven worker bound to an origin+path, HTTPS/localhost only, no DOM or synchronous XHR/Web Storage; it can intercept fetch and use Cache/IndexedDB. `scriptURL` and scope must be same-origin with page or registration throws SecurityError. Default scope is script directory; broader scope needs `Service-Worker-Allowed`. Sources: MDN https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Service_Worker_API ; register https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/ServiceWorkerContainer/register ; spec https://w3c.github.io/ServiceWorker/
- Lifecycle: download -> install -> waiting -> activate. A new worker normally waits until old controlled pages close; `skipWaiting()` accelerates activation and `clients.claim()` adopts open pages, but forcing both can make concurrently open control/stage windows run mismatched application code/state. For a live presentation, prefer version-cohort discipline and an explicit reload/update gate before session start; never hot-swap mid-session without protocol-version compatibility. Source: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Service_Worker_API/Using_Service_Workers
- Compatibility: registration Chrome 40+, Edge 17+, Firefox 44+, Safari 11.1+. Firefox private windows expose no `navigator.serviceWorker` (BCD note). Raw: https://github.com/mdn/browser-compat-data/blob/main/api/ServiceWorkerContainer.json and /Navigator.json
- Security architecture: separate stage origin gets its own narrowly scoped SW/cache, eliminating controller cookie/storage/cache exposure. Do not cache presentation secrets or authenticated API responses by default. Offline shell/assets do not make cloud AI or WSS available offline; communicate this distinction.

G. INSTALLABILITY
- Chromium manifest promotion requirements documented by MDN: name or short_name; 192px+512px icons; start_url; display/display_override; prefer_related_applications absent/false. A service worker is NOT universally an install prerequisite. MDN: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Progressive_web_apps/Guides/Making_PWAs_installable
- Chrome removed fetch-handler requirement for menu installation in Chrome 108 mobile / 112 desktop; empty fetch handlers hurt performance. Source: https://developer.chrome.com/blog/update-install-criteria
- `beforeinstallprompt` is non-standard/Limited, Chromium/Edge only (BCD Chrome 44+, Firefox/Safari false). It has no guaranteed fire time. Hide custom Install UI until event arrives; retain it, `preventDefault()`, call prompt from explicit user click; provide platform instructions elsewhere. MDN: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/beforeinstallprompt_event ; raw BCD https://github.com/mdn/browser-compat-data/blob/main/api/BeforeInstallPromptEvent.json
- Desktop: Chromium installs manifest PWAs; Safari 17/macOS Sonoma Add to Dock can install any website with/without manifest; desktop Firefox does not install manifest PWAs. Mobile: Android major browsers install; iOS <=16.3 Safari only; iOS 16.4+ Share menu can be offered by third-party browsers, though all use WebKit. MDN install guide above; WebKit macOS source https://webkit.org/blog/14445/webkit-features-in-safari-17-0/ ; iOS source https://webkit.org/blog/13966/webkit-features-in-safari-16-4/ ; Edge https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/progressive-web-apps/how-to/
- Installation and Window Management are independent. Installing on Firefox/Safari does not add multi-screen placement; installing in Chromium does not eliminate permission/user-gesture/popup rules.

H. RECOMMENDED CAPABILITY TIERS
Tier 0 all modern secure browsers: editor/controller, WSS sync, mic where granted, explicit stage open, manual drag/fullscreen, offline shell when SW supported.
Tier 1 Chromium desktop: `isExtended/getScreenDetails`, permission-guided automatic placement, screen-change recovery, optionally targeted fullscreen.
Tier 2 installed PWA: standalone controller window, OS launcher integration, cached shell/assets; still do capability detection and still require mic/window/fullscreen permissions/gestures.
Security boundary: trusted `app.example` = setup/controller/presenter/mic/AI; public `stage.example` = rendered state only, read-only short-lived WSS capability, separate storage/SW, no broad cookies. Strict COOP sacrifices focus/closed and uses WSS presence; moderate compatible COOP retains restricted lifecycle handle.

Major product copy constraints: never claim 'works on any browser' for automatic dual-screen; say 'automatic multi-display setup on Chromium desktop; guided manual setup elsewhere.' Never claim 'offline AI'; say 'app shell and prepared assets can remain available offline.' Never show universal in-app install button; feature-detect or show browser-specific instructions.
summary: Sourced PWA/browser capability report and architecture implications
